previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, poorly controlled due to medication noncompliance, alcohol use disorder, and depression, presented with altered mental status and was found to be in severe diabetic ketoacidosis with a glucose of 1214, pH of 6.92, and anion gap of 56. She had hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury with creatinine rising to 2.8, and hypotension requiring pressor support. Due to worsening acidosis and respiratory fatigue, she was intubated and admitted to the MICU. She received an insulin drip, IV fluids, bicarbonate, and temporary hemodialysis via a right internal jugular line. Her course improved with correction of metabolic abnormalities, and she was transitioned to subcutaneous insulin. She had a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction likely due to demand ischemia, managed medically with metoprolol, aspirin, and atorvastatin. Psychiatry initiated Zoloft and arranged for a dual-diagnosis partial hospitalization program. Her renal function recovered, and she was discharged home with services, improved mental status, and a plan for ongoing behavioral and medical follow-up.

#Depression and Substance Abuse: Pt presented to hospital from 
an outpatient partial program that she was discharged to on her

Psychiatry also saw the patient to determine if poor glycemic 
control is due to depression or cognitive impairment. They noted 
that she scored poorly on a MOCA with a score of ___, which 
makes her significantly impaired. This impairment was believed 
to have been due to many years of DM-1 and alcohol abuse. They 
recommended restructuring of her diabetes regimen, increased ___ 
support (twice a day visits) and increased family involvement. 
They also commented that Ms. ___ would not benefit from 
psychiatric inpatient level of care. They further recommended 
that OT be consulted to determine the functional level of her 
cognitive impairment and a SW consult to make sure the patient 
is able to return to the ___ PHP and family work. Finally, 
they asked that she be maintained on her sertraline 100mg QD.

#DKA: Unknown trigger as pt denied alcohol use and serum EtOH 
was negative in the ED. Patient's diabetes is historically 
poorly controlled. Initial lab results were consistent with DKA 
(metabolic acidosis, anion gap 44, glucose 810, lactate 3.5) Ms. 
___ was treated per DKA protocol with IVF, an insulin drip, 
and repletion of electrolytes as necessary. A ___ consult was 
called and recommended 16U lantus at breakfast and sliding scale 
with 3 start at FSBG of 71 and increasingly by 2U/50mg. 

#Hypotension: Pt was hypotensive in ED (80s systolics), but BP 
responded well to to fluid resuscitation. Concern for sepsis was 
low given no symptoms of infection. Her initial chest xray was 
clear. One set of blood cultures grew gram positive cocci in 
clusters, species coag neagtive staphh in only one set thought 
to be secondary to contamination. The patient was started on 
vancomycin for broad spectrum gram positive coverage on ___ that 
was subsequently stopped on ___ due to resolution of hypotension 
and no infectious symptoms. 

___: Creat was 2.2 on admission (elevated from baseline of 
around 0.6), likely pre-renal ___ dehydration from DKA. With 
resolution of DKA and hydration with IVF, patient's Cr returned 
to baseline of 0.5-0.6. 

#Troponinemia: Troponin T 0.04 in ED with questionable ST 
changes on EKG in V3-V5, and once in ICU troponins were stable 
at 0.03. Pt denied any chest pain. Likely demand ischemia and 
not due to acute coronary artery occlusion. The patient was 
continued on her home doses of ASA and atorvastatin. Troponins 
leveled off at 0.03. 

#Leukocytosis: Most likely a stress response. Normalized with 
treatment of DKA.

#Nausea/Vomiting: Likely ___ DKA. Refractory to Zofran, but 
improved with Ativan and treatment of underlying issue (DKA).

#Anemia: Mildly anemic w/ Hgb 9.3 and MCV 95 with a wide RDW 
likely reflective of a mixed microcytic and macrocytic anemia. 
Stable from prior admission where she was found to have 
macrocytic anemia and prescribed folate and thiamine on 
discharge. Thiamine and folate were continued on this admission.
